To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have established a cellular model of TDP-42 aggregation based on its C-terminal Gln-rich region, which is involved in the aggregation and recruitment of endogenous TDP43.

the introduction of tandem repetitions of TDP43 C-terminal Gln-rich region in cell lines and rat primary neuronal culture triggers the formation of phosphorylation and ubiquitination of aggregates that recapitulates many but not all of the characteristics observed in the disease.
tandem repeats of TDP-4331–369 can induce the formation of cellular aggregates that are able to recruit endogenous TTP-43.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular characterization of the TDP-43 protein and the elucidation of the role of this protein in the formation of aggregates in neurodegenerative disorders such as ALS.
the identification of the mechanisms that lead to the formation of TDP- 43 aggregates and the development of novel strategies to prevent/reduce their formation.

the study of the molecular mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis of amyotrophic lateral slerosis (ALS), which is a neurodegenerative disease characterized by progressive loss of upper and lower motor neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have developed a cellular model of TDP-42 aggregation that recapitulates many but not all of the characteristics observed in ALS and FTDL patients, and this model can be useful for the investigation of the mechanisms involved in TDP-43 inclusions and for the development of therapeutic strategies to prevent/reduce TDP-43 aggregates.
we have established a cell-based Tdp-43 aggregation model, which will be useful to test therapeutic strategies/effecters aimed at preventing/reduction of this phenomenon.

this study establishes a cell-based model of TDP- 43 aggregation that recapitulates many but not all features observed in patients and will be useful to study the mechanisms of TDP-42 aggregation and the gain- of-function consequences of TPD-43 aggregation within the cell.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the C-terminal region of TDP- 43, which contains the Q/N-rich region and the nuclear localization signal, is sufficient to drive the formation of TDP-42-positive aggregates in cells.

the C-terminal region of TDP- 43 is involved in its interaction with other proteins and in its aggregation process, and the latter is recapitulated in a cellular model that will help to understand the mechanisms underlying this process and to test new therapeutic strategies.
tandem repetitions of TDP43 331-369 induce cellular aggregates which recruit endogenous TPD-43.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have established a cell-based Tdp-43 aggregation model based on the introduction of tandem repetitions of its C-terminal Gln-rich region.
the Gln/Asparagine-rich region of TDP- 43 is a key player in the formation of TDP-42 aggregates.

the introduction of a tandem repeat carrying the C-terminal GQ-rich region of TDP- 43 is sufficient to promote the formation of cellular aggregates that recruit TDP-43, and this model will be useful for the development of strategies to reduce TDP-43 inclusions.
